partners.mechanism_chain: USP9X (HGNC:12727) —DISRUPTS→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-909733); USP9X (HGNC:12727) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); SKI (HGNC:10237) —DECREASES→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-909733); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-909733) —LEADS_TO→ Craniosynostosis (HP:0000238). Loss-of-function mutations in USP9X (n1), a deubiquitinase, impair its ability to regulate protein stability and signaling pathways. One critical pathway affected is TGF-beta signaling (n2), which is crucial for neurodevelopment and connective tissue formation. Disruption of USP9X function directly leads to intellectual disability (n3). In Shprintzen-Goldberg syndrome, while USP9X is also implicated, mutations in SKI (n5), a negative regulator of TGF-beta signaling, or potentially USP9X itself, lead to dysregulation of the TGF-beta pathway, resulting in phenotypes such as craniosynostosis (n4) and other connective tissue abnormalities characteristic of SGS.
